clue.text: Notice only change

blocks.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
just means only, as in 'just one'

explanation.surface: An instruction to observe and alter nothing else, like a minimal editing note.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something is to alter it slightly, a synonym of the verb change.

clue.text: Having started a course

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who has enrolled in a course of study or medicine
setter's reading: racehorses that have left the stalls and set off round the course

explanation.walkthrough: The course sounds like a class or a course of pills; it is a racecourse, and commentators say the runners are this word once the race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing commentators say 'they're off' or this word when horses have left the start and are under way.

clue.text: Unorthodox Jews have this son, one preaching the Second Coming

indicators.note: unorthodox means departing from the usual form, so the letters that follow are not kept in their usual order

blocks.note: fifteen letters of fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a nonconformist Jewish family whose son has become an evangelist.
explanation.walkthrough: The religious surface fits the answer neatly, which hides that the first four words are simply letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this Christian denomination proclaim the imminent return of Christ, preaching door to door.

clue.text: Put whisky in front of the two swallowing drop of rice soup

indicators.note: in front of places the first item before what follows in the answer
a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the next word is used
something swallowing another takes it inside itself

blocks.note: Scotch is whisky from Scotland
both means the two of them
opening letter of rice

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: add whisky before the pair, catching a drop of rice in the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The soup is a thick Scottish broth of barley, vegetables and meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch broth is a traditional Scottish soup made with barley, mutton and vegetables.

clue.text: Work on, repeatedly dipping into drink

indicators.note: dipping into means going inside, so one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: often means repeatedly
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone keeps dunking something into a drink as they work on it, like a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften someone up is to work on them, weakening their resistance before asking something.

clue.text: Manage part of poem written in Old English

indicators.note: something written in another is set inside it

blocks.note: a verse is a section of a poem
OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English

explanation.surface: Handling a stanza of an Anglo-Saxon poem, as a scholar might.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or direct, a synonym of manage.

clue.text: Finest spinner

blocks.note: first meaning: best, highest quality
second meaning: a child's toy that spins on its point

explanation.walkthrough: Spinner suggests a cricket bowler, but here it is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for the best of something and a noun for a spinning toy.

clue.text: Warned cold nasty criminal in police HQ

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of their order

blocks.note: fifteen letters of fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A frosty, unpleasant crook gets a caution at the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: New Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the London Metropolitan Police's headquarters building.

clue.text: Salesman hung up, cut off, but didn't give up

indicators.note: in a down clue, hung up means lifted upward, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
severed means cut off

explanation.surface: A cold-calling salesman has the phone put down on him yet keeps trying.
explanation.walkthrough: Hung up and cut off both suggest a phone call ending, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to persist despite difficulty, the opposite of giving up.

clue.text: Disappear? That is in doubt, though bishop's missing

indicators.note: missing means absent, so that letter is dropped from the word
in places the first phrase inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether something will vanish, doubtful now that the bishop has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing B leaves DOUT, and IE goes in after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To die out is to become extinct, vanishing entirely, so it means disappear.

clue.text: The radio broadcast, about 11, exposes Greek goddess?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around another

blocks.note: taken as written
11-across is POWER, and P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A radio programme reveals something about a Greek goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 11 points to the answer at 11-across, whose abbreviation supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Energy authority

blocks.note: first meaning: electricity or energy supply
second meaning: control or influence over others

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an energy regulator; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both energy, as in electric supply, and authority, as in political control.

clue.text: Brutal mob in situation worsened by attempts to solve it

definitions.text: situation worsened by attempts to solve it

blocks.note: vicious means brutal
a circle is a group or set of people

explanation.surface: A violent gang is caught in a mess that every fix makes worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicious circle is a self-perpetuating cycle where each response aggravates the original problem.

clue.text: Opera lover at riot? Unlikely

indicators.note: unlikely suggests an improbable version, so the letters are made into an improbable arrangement

blocks.note: eleven letters of fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Doubt that an opera fan would be found at a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Il Trovatore is Verdi's opera, Italian for 'The Troubadour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Il Trovatore is an opera by Verdi first staged in 1853, so an example of the definition.

clue.text: Found under piece of debris one's put out

indicators.note: a piece is a small part, so just the first letter of the word is used
in a down clue, under places one part below, that is after, the other

blocks.note: opening letter of debris
one is I, plus the 's
found means located

explanation.surface: Someone discovered beneath rubble has a joint knocked out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an earthquake rescue; put out is the definition, as in a dislocated shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint that is put out has been displaced from its socket, so it is dislocated.

clue.text: Tenant wearing dress

definitions.note: used as a verb: to occupy as a tenant

blocks.note: dressed in something is wearing it
a habit is a garment, such as a nun's dress

explanation.surface: A lodger wearing a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenant looks like a noun but works as a verb meaning to occupy.
explanation.definitionFit: To tenant a place is to live in or occupy it, which is what inhabiting means.

clue.text: Section of government — it leaked name

indicators.note: a section is a portion cut from within, so the letters lie inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the end of the first word and the next two

explanation.surface: A government department let a name slip to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle something is to give it a title, that is to name it.

clue.text: Dope in an inferior position?

blocks.note: first meaning: inside information, slang for the facts
second meaning: placed low, beneath

explanation.walkthrough: Dope suggests drugs or a fool; it is slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means the inside story or facts; read as two words it means placed low.

clue.text: One proposed for election in old colliery in the north-east

indicators.note: in places the preceding phrase inside the region named after it

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a colliery is a coal mine
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A candidate standing in a former mining area of north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: The north-east of England was a coalfield region, so the surface reads as local politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward as a candidate for an office or award.

clue.text: Put in quarantine, one thus gets delayed

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
so means thus
late means delayed

explanation.surface: Someone placed in quarantine is consequently held up.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate someone is to keep them apart from others, as quarantine does.

clue.text: This cannot describe units I just repositioned

definitions.text: This cannot describe units I just repositioned

indicators.note: repositioned means moved to new places, so these letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what phrase cannot apply to items that have just been moved.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the anagram moves the letters, and things just moved are by definition no longer in their original place.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ means in the original place, so it cannot describe anything that has been moved.

clue.text: Make a favourable impression on the game colonel following snub

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the rest is placed behind the opening word

blocks.note: to cut someone is to snub them
taken as written
Colonel Mustard is a suspect in the board game Cluedo

explanation.surface: Someone snubbed tries to impress the colonel from a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo (Clue in North America) is a murder-mystery board game whose suspects include Colonel Mustard.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut the mustard is an idiom for succeeding or coming up to expectations.

clue.text: Emperor and son taken aboard by sailor

indicators.note: taken aboard means brought onto a ship, so one letter goes inside the other word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A ruler and his child are taken onto a ship by a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsar was the emperor of Russia before 1917.

clue.text: Topic during foot-and-mouth emergency

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters straddling the end of mouth and the start of emergency

explanation.surface: A subject discussed during a livestock disease outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: Foot-and-mouth is a contagious disease of cattle and sheep; a British outbreak in 2001 was a national emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a discussion or work.

clue.text: Make a mistake with bishop, bringing on end of game

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: last letter of game
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A chess player blunders with the bishop, hastening the endgame.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop suggests B from chess, but here it is RR, Right Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, as in 'to err is human'.

clue.text: Natives — number abandoned on it, alas

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for number
taken as written

explanation.surface: Locals lament that a number was left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Abandoned looks like it means left behind; it is the anagram signal in its sense of unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationals are citizens of a country, as natives are those born there.

clue.text: Rat in waste, rolling about

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the word for about is read backwards

blocks.note: a desert is a waste, a barren area
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A rodent tumbles about in wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: Rat looks like the animal but means a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is someone who betrays or abandons their side, just as a deserter does.

clue.text: Drinking spree in makeshift shelter

blocks.note: first meaning: a heavy drinking session
second meaning: a tent of bent branches covered with tarpaulin

explanation.walkthrough: A bender is British slang for a drinking binge, and also a traveller's shelter of bent saplings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bout of heavy drinking and a dome-shaped tent of bent poles.
